transcript: I go to a lot of theatre, but never had I been to a show where they constructed a swimming pool for skateboarding as the primary set piece. In Bowl EP, we primarily follow two people drinking, flirting, skating and rapping their way into a small but passionate are-we-aren't-we kind of thing. This play is episodic in nature, and initially is very slow to reveal information about the characters, sparingly alluding to their backstories here and there. The focus is mostly on their mundane but chemistry-charged interactions as they grow closer. Later, a bunch of crazy stuff goes down that makes things a whole lot more confusing but eventually sheds light on the dynamic of the main pair. I liked this show a lot more in retrospect once I was able to form some sort of interpretation, but it was a bit of a hard watch in the moment. I guess I kept trying to find my bearings and contextualize things, and at seemingly every turn, it just didn't really provide me information in a way that I generally expect narratives to do so. But I think in a lot of ways, its form and the experience it induced in me as an audience member was both as intended and reflective of the themes of the piece itself — messy, edgy, and pushing things to the edge. Bowl EP is running at Vineyard Theatre through June 15th. With that, another program for my collection.
